reverse_expectations.model: 10-year constant owner-cash-per-share growth followed by terminal owner-cash multiple
reverse_expectations.interpretation: At a 10% required return and 16x terminal owner-cash multiple, the current price requires essentially zero owner-cash/share growth for ten years. Even if normalized owner-cash margin compresses to 25%, implied growth is only about 3%. This is a substantial expectation gap if Adobe can retain professional-workflow economics through the AI transition.

permanent_loss_stress.assumptions: Owner cash/share -8% CAGR years 1-5 and -2% years 6-10; 12% discount; 9x terminal. General AI/Figma/Canva own the interface, Adobe becomes a lower-value backend utility, pricing and seats compress.

bear.assumptions: Owner cash/share -3% CAGR years 1-5 then flat; 11% discount; 12x terminal. AI monetization largely cannibalizes existing spend and professional workflow share erodes.

base.assumptions: Owner cash/share +6% CAGR years 1-5 and +5% years 6-10; 10% discount; 17x terminal. Adobe retains workflow control, AI becomes a paid attach/ARPU driver, but growth normalizes well below recent revenue/ARR rates.

bull.assumptions: Owner cash/share +10% CAGR years 1-5 and +8% years 6-10; 9% discount; 20x terminal. Firefly/Acrobat AI/CX Enterprise strengthen Adobe's system-of-record role and expand paid users/ARPU across creativity, productivity and enterprise marketing.

warnings: Scenario fair values are decision ranges, not price targets.
AI-driven moat uncertainty is more important than small changes in terminal multiple.
Mechanical OCF-capex is not used as owner cash because it adds back SBC; central owner cash keeps SBC as a real economic expense.
